notes: aids: an element is a reading aid when its type and supertype, each trimmed and folded as the room profile defines it, are one of pairs, and it carries mark.field, read by presence: any value but null, a string only when something is left after trimming White_Space, an empty list or an empty object never (serial 126). The pair without the mark is lore; the mark on no pair makes nothing. Wherever a type is compared to a kind (a pair, a hub's kind, a skill's being an Object), it is trimmed and folded as the room profile defines it.

element: isCharterElement(element), in the room profile's matcher-case shape: element gives type, supertype and the mark as a body might carry them; is_charter_element is what the reader must answer, the pair AND the mark. A mark counts when its value is not null: a string only when something is left after the White_Space trim, an empty list or an empty object as absent, any other value (a number, a list or an object with something in it) as present; the value is never compared.

worlds: each world's elements as its owner is served them, the ids its hidden mark keeps from every reader but a keeper (the owner or a co-builder) and the one who made each, and its readers, in the lens fixture's shape. A reader's rung is owner (the whole world), contributor (the world less the hidden, plus each hidden element its whole lists, which is one it made, as a guest's whole lists its own creation), guest (exactly the whole and known_of ids it lists; known_of is a stub, served as the lens profile serves one: its id, type, name, description, supertype, subtype and image_url, the server's times and its type's public fields, no link and no extension field) or public (the world less the hidden and the room elements, and nothing at all unless the world carries open: true, a world open to anyone). A case's world is a name in worlds or, as a graph case's is, a world of its own.

a stub's standing: a stub serves no extension field, so whether an element the reader holds only as a stub is a reading aid is read from the element as the owner is served it; what the reading shows of it is what the stub serves.

charter: want is charterOf(world, reader). charter is {id, type, name, rules, skill} or null, type law: the newest marked Charter the reader sees, by created_at compared as instants (none sorts oldest), then the higher id by code point; rules the rules_field list as stored, [] when absent or null; skill the ids its description names (any id written as 8-4-4-4-12 hex, so every ow:// form, a site address and a bare id), in lowercase, each once in the order written, kept when it is an Object of this world the reader sees (served whole to every reader who reads the Charter; one the hidden mark keeps from the reader is not seen and not kept), the first skill_max of those kept. guide is {id, type, name} or null, type construct, chosen the same way among marked Guides. domains is every marked Domain the reader sees, each {id, type, name, sentence, hubs}, type construct: in the order of the Guide's constructs as the reader is served them first (an id named twice keeps its first place, an entry that is no marked Domain is skipped), then the rest by folded name and then id; with no Guide seen, by folded name and id alone. A name is trimmed and folded as the room profile defines it. Folded names compare by code point, as written: never by UTF-16 unit, a collation or a locale, and nothing is normalized before or after the fold, so a decomposed and a precomposed spelling are two names.

sentence: the description as served, trimmed of White_Space at both ends, cut at its first line break (a line feed or a carriage return) and trimmed again, so its first line that holds something; an empty string when there is none. hubs: the distinct {type, id} the Domain's served link fields name, each an element of its field's kind in the reader's view (any other id names no hub), in hub_fields' order (the Construct's link fields, the schema's order) and each list's own order, the Domain itself excluded; a stub serves no links, so a stub Domain's hubs are [].
compare: objects are compared as values; the order of keys carries no meaning, so a reader that writes {type, id} or {id, type, name} in another order answers the same.

design_cases: each case is a world of its own, a reader and want, every design part the reader sees: an Object or a Construct the reader is served whole (a known-of stub has none, though it is served its subtype) whose subtype, trimmed and folded as the room profile defines it, is in design or locked, in a world where charterOf finds a Charter for that reader; each {type, id, state}, type object or construct and state the page's word (in design or locked), whatever the spelling stored. want compares as a set.

mark.value: the id of the world the aid was written for; read by presence, never by its value

cases.name: harbour-owner-reads-the-whole-packet
cases.note: The newest marked Charter (the unmarked, newer one is lore); its skill in text order, the hidden Object kept for the owner; the Guide's order with a doubled entry once and a lore Construct skipped; then the two Domains the Guide does not name, by folded name; each sentence cut at the first line break (a carriage return in the Docks) and trimmed; a Domain's link to itself is no hub.

cases.name: harbour-contributor-a-hidden-domain-and-hub-are-not-there
cases.note: The Vault and the Sealed Orders are hidden: the Vault is not listed and nothing marks the gap, the Orders are neither skill nor hub.

cases.name: harbour-guest-the-charter-whole-its-skill-whole-a-stub-domain-a-name
cases.note: The Charter whole to a guest (the keeper's house rules), its skill Objects served whole beside it, as to every reader who reads the Charter, and kept; the Lighthouse a stub: its name and served sentence, no hubs; a hub outside the guest's slice left out; ash row, which names the guest's own Character, is in its slice and listed after the Guide's order; Domains the guest does not see are not listed.

cases.name: a-public-reader-on-a-closed-world-reads-nothing
cases.note: The Charter is the public's only on a world open to anyone.

cases.name: two-charters-at-one-instant-the-higher-id-a-guide-with-no-created-at-the-oldest
cases.note: The two Charters were made at one instant, written in two offsets: the higher id by code point leads. The Guide with no created_at sorts oldest, under a higher id. Rules B's rules are not read, Rules A has none: [].

cases.name: the-pairs-without-the-mark-are-lore
cases.note: A Charter, a Guide and a Domain with no mark are lore; the mark on no pair, or on a word that only resembles one (Domains), makes no reading aid.

cases.name: the-mark-by-presence-trimmed-as-the-room-profile-trims
cases.note: A mark naming another world counts (presence, never its value) and the pair is trimmed and folded; a mark of a no-break space and a space is blank, so the newer Law is lore; a mark of U+001F is a mark (not White_Space); an empty mark is none.

cases.name: a-guide-the-owner-sees-orders-the-domains
cases.note: The Guide is hidden from every reader but the owner, who reads its order.

cases.name: no-guide-seen-the-domains-by-folded-name-and-id
cases.note: No Guide this reader sees: the Domains by folded name, then id (north and " North " fold alike, the lower id first); the guide is null.

cases.name: a-public-reader-on-an-open-world
cases.note: Open to anyone: the public reads the Charter, the Guide and the Domains it sees, less the hidden and the room elements (no skill, no hub, no Domain from either).

cases.name: an-open-world-read-by-its-owner
cases.note: The owner's reading of the same world: the hidden Domain after the Guide's, the hidden Object and the room line as hubs in the schema's field order.

cases.name: skill-each-id-once-in-order-objects-of-this-world-the-first-five
cases.note: Every form in one text: each id once in the order written (an uppercase id read in lowercase), kept only as an Object of this world (the world's own id, a Character and another world's Object dropped), the first five of those kept.

cases.name: skill-the-five-are-counted-after-the-cut
cases.note: The Tongs are hidden from this reader: cut first, so the sixth Object written comes in.

cases.name: skill-form-ow-object
cases.note: One form alone; a world carried by the case, as a graph case does.

cases.name: skill-form-cross-world

cases.note: One form alone; a world carried by the case, as a graph case does.

cases.note: The guest knows the Guide only as a stub, a name and an id: it is still the Guide, answered as {id, type, name}. A stub serves no links, so its constructs order nothing: the Domains the guest sees come by folded name and id alone, ash row first, where the Guide's stored order would put the Archive and the Docks first.

cases.name: a-proposed-charter-is-no-readers-charter
cases.note: A proposed element is in no reader's view, the owner's included (one whose x_review_proposed counts as present by the review profile's rule 1, a seat's mark or a doubt; an empty mark is settled): the newer Charter and Guide are proposed, so the settled ones lead; the Annex carries a doubt and is no Domain; the Draft Ledger is proposed, so it is kept neither in the skill nor in the Hall's hubs.

cases.name: a-member-reading-the-charter-as-a-stub-reads-it-whole
cases.note: The guest's slice holds the Charter only as a known-of stub, which serves no extension field: the Charter is every member rung's to read whole, so its rules and its skill come from the Charter itself, not from the stub.

cases.name: a-skill-id-compares-as-a-uuid-whatever-its-case
cases.note: An id found in the text is taken in lowercase, in whichever case it is written: the Object written in uppercase hex and again in lowercase is one Object, kept once, in lowercase.

cases.name: a-skill-id-named-only-in-uppercase-is-kept
cases.note: The only copy of the skill's id in the Charter's text is in uppercase hex: a reader that compares the text as written finds no such Object and drops it; read as a UUID it is the Object, kept, in lowercase.

cases.name: a-charter-with-an-empty-object-mark-is-settled-and-leads
cases.note: The newer Charter's x_review_proposed is an empty object, {}: an empty mark, which counts as no proposal by the review profile's rule 1, so the newer Charter is settled and leads.

cases.name: a-charter-with-an-empty-string-mark-is-settled-and-leads
cases.note: The newer Charter's x_review_proposed is an empty string, "": an empty mark, which counts as no proposal by the review profile's rule 1, so the newer Charter is settled and leads.

cases.name: a-domains-sentence-trims-before-it-cuts-so-a-leading-line-break-is-passed-over

elements.name: The Docks
elements.description:
Where the ferries tie up.  
And the tar sheds.

cases.note: The sentence is the description trimmed of White_Space, cut at its first line break and trimmed again: the two leading line feeds and the spaces go with the first trim, so the sentence is the first line that holds something, trimmed. A reader that cuts before it trims answers an empty sentence here and is red.

cases.name: a-domains-sentence-of-white-space-and-line-breaks-alone-is-the-empty-string
cases.note: A description of White_Space and line breaks alone leaves nothing after the trim: the sentence is the empty string, never null and never a key left out.

cases.name: a-skill-object-whose-own-id-is-in-upper-case-is-not-kept
cases.note: The Charter names both Objects in lowercase; the Ledger's own id is held in upper case. An id found in the text is taken in lowercase and matched as written against the world's Objects (the address profile's "The same id"), so the Ledger is not kept and the Map is. A reader that folds the case of the Objects' ids too keeps both.

cases.name: a-skill-id-is-found-wherever-it-stands-in-the-text
cases.note: Five Objects, each named once in the form: with a hex digit before it, with one after it, inside a word, in braces, after urn:uuid:. An id found in a text is the form wherever it stands, whatever stands before it or after it (the address profile's "The same id"): all five are kept, in the order written. A reader that asks for a boundary around the id keeps fewer.

cases.name: two-ids-that-share-characters-the-first-found-is-kept
cases.note: The text holds 64 characters of id: the first form is its first 36, and a second form begins at the first's 29th character (the first's last eight digits, then the rest). A text is read from its start and the characters of one id found are part of no other (the address profile's "The same id"), so only the first is found. Both are Objects of the world: the Ledger is kept, the Map is not. A reader that tries every position in the text keeps both.

cases.name: two-ids-that-share-characters-the-second-alone-is-not-found
cases.note: The text holds 64 characters of id: the first form is its first 36, and a second form begins at the first's 29th character (the first's last eight digits, then the rest). A text is read from its start and the characters of one id found are part of no other (the address profile's "The same id"), so only the first is found. Only the second is an Object of the world: the first names nothing, and the second's characters still belong to it, so nothing is kept. A reader that looks for a second id where the first names nothing keeps the Map.

cases.name: two-charters-at-one-instant-the-higher-id-as-written-leads
cases.note: Two Charters at one instant, their ids 019B7F00-... and 019a7f00-...: the higher id by code point leads, of the ids as written, and a lowercase a comes after an upper-case B, so Rules A leads. A reader that folds the case first reads 019b above 019a and puts Rules B first.

cases.name: a-created-at-with-no-offset-is-read-as-utc
cases.note: Rules A's created_at has no offset and is read as UTC, 10:00 UTC; Rules B's is 09:30 UTC. The instant puts A later, so A leads, where a comparison of the text puts B later, and so does a reader that reads a time with no offset as its own local time east of UTC. B has the higher id. The case cannot catch a reader whose own clock is UTC.

cases.name: a-created-at-that-is-a-date-alone-is-read-as-absent
cases.note: Rules, dated by day, carries the created_at 2026-11-12, a date with no time, which is not the one form a created_at is read in: it is read as absent and sorts as the oldest, so the older readable Rules leads. A reader that hands the text to its language's own parser may read it as that day's midnight and put it first.

cases.name: charter-empty-list-mark-is-none
cases.note: The newer Law's x_charter_of is an empty list, []: no mark, as the review profile reads an empty mark (a compact reader leaves it out), so the newer Law is lore and the older Charter leads.

cases.name: charter-empty-object-mark-is-none
cases.note: The newer Law's x_charter_of is an empty object, {}: no mark, as the review profile reads an empty mark (a compact reader leaves it out), so the newer Law is lore and the older Charter leads.

cases.name: an-id-of-another-kind-or-of-no-element-in-a-link-field-names-no-hub
cases.note: A folder may hold this: the Domain's characters name the Pier and the Breakwater, two Locations, and an id of no element; its locations name the Pier. A hub is an element of the kind its link field links to, in the reader's view: the Pier is one hub, location, from locations; the Breakwater, a Location named only in characters, is no hub, and neither is the id that names nothing. Whether such a link should exist is not this reader's question.

cases.name: a-charter-whose-type-is-stored-padded-and-capitalised-says-law
cases.note: The Law's type is stored as ' Law ', a space each side: trimmed and folded it is the pair, so it is the Charter, and the packet says the pair's own word, law, never the spelling stored.

cases.name: a-domain-whose-type-is-stored-in-capitals-says-construct
cases.note: The Construct's type is stored as CONSTRUCT: folded it is the pair, so it is a Domain, and the packet says construct.

cases.name: a-hub-location-whose-type-is-stored-padded-is-a-hub
cases.note: The Net Loft's type is stored as ' Location ', a space each side: compared to the field's kind trimmed and folded, as the room profile defines it, it is a Location, so it is a hub, typed location, never the spelling stored.

cases.name: a-skill-object-whose-type-is-stored-capitalised-is-kept
cases.note: The Runbook's type is stored as Object: compared to object trimmed and folded, as the room profile defines it, it is an Object of this world, so the Charter keeps it in skill.

cases.name: types-are-trimmed-and-folded-by-the-room-profile-not-by-a-language
cases.note: The answer is the room profile's (its trim, the White_Space set, and its fold, simple case folding by the C and S rows), never a language's own. Domains: an ideographic space each side of construct is trimmed (a Domain); con + U+FB06 + ruct is not construct, since the ligature has no simple folding (no Domain; a full fold would make one); CON + U+017F + TRUCT folds to construct, the long s to s (a Domain; lower-casing leaves it). Hubs: U+FEFF before Location is no White_Space, so the type is not location (no hub; a trim that takes a byte order mark would make one); location + U+001F likewise (no hub; a trim that takes the unit separator would make one); an em space, U+2003, before LOCATION is trimmed and the word folds (a hub). Birch Row is no Domain, so the order is Alder Quay, Cinder Point.

cases.name: folded-names-compare-by-code-point-so-an-astral-letter-comes-after-a-full-width-one
cases.note: No Guide: the Domains by folded name, then id. U+10400, a capital beyond U+FFFF, folds to U+10428, so three names fold alike and go by id; the full-width A folds to U+FF41. Compared by code point, U+FF41 and U+FF5A come before U+10428; a reader that compares UTF-16 units puts the three first, since a surrogate is below U+FF41.

cases.name: a-sharp-s-has-no-simple-folding-so-it-is-ordered-as-written
cases.note: No Guide: the Domains by folded name, then id. U+00DF, the sharp s, has no simple folding and stays itself, after every ASCII letter; U+1E9E, the capital sharp s, folds to it, so those two fold alike and go by id. Full folding, which takes the sharp s to ss, orders them otherwise.

cases.name: a-decomposed-and-a-precomposed-name-are-two-names-ordered-as-written
cases.note: No Guide: the Domains by folded name, then id, as written. The first name is E followed by U+0301, a combining acute accent; the second is U+00C9, the precomposed capital E with acute. Nothing is normalized, so they are two names: the first folds to e followed by U+0301 and comes after Ecluse, the second folds to U+00E9 and comes after Zed.

cases.name: names-equal-after-folding-are-ordered-by-id
cases.note: No Guide: the Domains by folded name, then id. A long s, capitals and spaces at both ends: all four names trim and fold to pass, so they go by id alone, whatever their spelling as stored.

cases.name: a-byte-order-mark-before-a-name-or-a-unit-separator-after-it-stays-in-the-order
cases.note: No Guide: the Domains by folded name, then id, each name trimmed of White_Space and folded as the room profile defines it. U+FEFF, the byte order mark, and U+001F, the unit separator, have no White_Space property: the trim keeps them, so the first name comes after Cove, U+FEFF being above every letter here, and the second after Bay, U+001F being below every letter. A language's own trim may take either (JavaScript's trim takes the byte order mark, Python's strip the unit separator), and the name then ties with Bay and goes first by id.

cases.name: names-trimmed-of-a-next-line-or-an-ideographic-space-are-ordered-by-id
cases.note: No Guide: the Domains by folded name, then id, each name trimmed of White_Space and folded as the room profile defines it. U+0085, the next line character, and U+3000, the ideographic space, have the White_Space property: the trim takes them, so three names are bay and go by id, before Bayou. A trim that leaves U+0085 (JavaScript's, or one of the code points up to U+0020) or U+3000 (one up to U+0020, or one of the White_Space code points below U+0100) orders those names apart, after Bayou.

cases.name: names-equal-after-trimming-and-folding-are-ordered-by-id-whatever-their-created-at
cases.note: No Guide: the Domains by folded name, then id, and nothing else. The three names fold to heath; their created_at are in neither the order of their ids nor its reverse, so a reader that breaks the tie by created_at, oldest or newest first, before the id orders them otherwise.

cases.name: a-folded-name-that-another-begins-with-comes-before-it
cases.note: No Guide: the Domains by folded name, then id, the name compared first and whole. ash is the start of ash grove, so it comes first, whatever the ids. A reader that sorts one key made of the folded name and the id joined puts Ash Grove first, since the space after ash is below every character an id is written with.

cases.name: names-equal-after-folding-are-ordered-by-their-ids-as-written-never-folded
cases.note: No Guide: the Domains by folded name, then id, the ids as written. Mere and mere fold alike; their ids are 019A7F00-...-B502 and 019a7f00-...-b501. Compared as written, by code point, an upper-case A comes before a lowercase a, so Mere leads; a reader that folds the case of the ids first reads b501 below b502 and puts mere first. Moor comes last by its name.

cases.name: a-name-that-another-begins-with-before-a-control-character-comes-before-it
cases.note: No Guide: the Domains by folded name, then id, the name compared first and whole. The first name is Ash followed by U+0001, a control character with no White_Space property, so the trim keeps it; ash is the start of it, so Ash comes first, whatever the ids. A reader that sorts one key made of the folded name, a separator below U+001F and the id joined puts the longer name first whenever the separator is above U+0000.

design_cases.name: a-locked-object-in-a-world-with-a-charter-is-a-design-part
design_cases.note: The world's Charter carries the mark: the Object's subtype locked is its design state.

design_cases.name: a-construct-in-design-is-a-design-part
design_cases.note: A Construct carries the state as an Object does; no list of kinds decides it.

design_cases.name: a-subtype-with-a-capital-and-a-trailing-space-is-in-design
design_cases.note: The subtype is trimmed and folded as the room profile defines it; the state is the page's word, never the spelling stored.

design_cases.name: a-deprecated-construct-is-no-design-part
design_cases.note: A world's own further subtype is an ordinary subtype: no design state.

design_cases.name: a-law-with-a-subtype-is-no-design-part
design_cases.note: Only an Object or a Construct has a design state.

design_cases.name: a-locked-object-in-a-world-whose-charter-has-no-mark-is-no-design-part
design_cases.note: The world's only Law with supertype Charter has no mark, so charterOf finds no Charter and no element has a design state: locked is a word any world may use.

design_cases.name: a-workshops-spec-in-design-is-a-design-part
design_cases.note: The Construct is a room element (the room profile's pair construct + Spec, and the room's mark, which holds its sitting's id as a workshop's element does; the sitting's own mark holds the world's id): no kind is excluded, so its subtype in design is its design state in a world with a Charter.

design_cases.name: a-locked-law-is-no-design-part
design_cases.note: Only an Object or a Construct has a design state: a Law whose subtype is locked, in a world with a Charter, is no design part.

design_cases.name: a-locked-object-with-a-unit-separator-after-it-has-no-design-state
design_cases.note: The subtype is locked followed by U+001F, the unit separator, which has no White_Space property: the room profile's trim leaves it, so the trimmed subtype is no design state (a language's own trim may take it).

design_cases.name: a-locked-object-a-guest-holds-only-as-a-stub-has-no-design-state
design_cases.note: The guest reads the marked Charter whole and holds the Object only as a known-of stub, which is served its subtype locked (the lens profile): the state is read only from an element served whole, so the stub has none.

design_cases.name: a-hidden-charter-gives-its-owner-a-design-part
design_cases.note: The world's marked Charter carries the hidden mark. Its owner sees it, so the locked Object is a design part for the owner. The next case is the same world read by a contributor.

design_cases.name: a-hidden-charter-gives-a-contributor-no-design-part
design_cases.note: The same world as the case before, read by a contributor: the hidden mark keeps the Charter from it, and it wins over rule 5, so charterOf finds no Charter for this reader and the locked Object, which it reads whole, has no design state.

design_cases.name: a-part-whose-type-is-stored-with-spaces-and-a-capital-is-written-object
design_cases.note: The Object's type is stored as " Object ": trimmed and folded it is an Object, and its type in the answer is object, the kind's own word, as the packet writes a type.

design_cases.name: a-hidden-locked-object-is-no-design-part-for-a-contributor
design_cases.note: The marked Charter is the contributor's to read, and the locked Object carries the hidden mark: the contributor is not served the Object, so it reads no design state on it. Its owner, served it whole, would read it as a design part.

design_cases.name: a-hidden-charter-gives-the-contributor-who-made-it-a-design-part
design_cases.note: The Charter carries the hidden mark and was made by the maker, a contributor, whose whole lists it: the hidden mark keeps an element from every reader but a keeper and the one who made it (the lens profile's rule 1), so charterOf finds the Charter for the maker, and the locked Object it reads whole is a design part.

design_cases.name: a-charter-a-guest-holds-only-as-a-stub-opens-the-gate
design_cases.note: The guest holds the marked Charter only as a known-of stub and the locked Object whole: the Charter is every member rung's to read whole, a known-of stub included (rule 5), so charterOf finds it for the guest and the Object is a design part.

design_cases.name: an-object-locked-between-two-next-line-characters-is-locked
design_cases.note: The subtype is locked with U+0085, the next line character, before and after it. U+0085 has the White_Space property, so the room profile's trim takes it and the state is locked (a language's own trim may leave it).

design_cases.name: a-locked-object-after-a-byte-order-mark-has-no-design-state
design_cases.note: The subtype is locked after U+FEFF, the byte order mark, which has no White_Space property: the room profile's trim keeps it, so the trimmed subtype is no design state (a language's own trim may take it).

design_cases.name: a-construct-in-design-written-with-a-long-s-is-in-design
design_cases.note: The subtype is in design with its s written as U+017F, the long s. Simple case folding takes the long s to s, so the state is in design (a language's lower-casing leaves the long s as it is).
